propositions: A write whose lock acquisition times out is permanently discarded without retry, losing data when holder duration exceeds the budget.
The acquire() function computes a single deadline as timeout * attempts and polls without fairness, so attempts is a silent multiplier not a retry loop.
Holder durations of 70s to 163s routinely exceed the 60s budget, causing all waiting writers to lose their appends with zero durable record.
Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() with per-pass warnings and cumulative wait tracking converts lock timeouts from permanent loss into latency.
The retry loop is safe against double-append because LockTimeout is raised before the caller's write body runs and cannot re-enter the acquisition.
Five call sites opt into retries via write_path_retries() reading REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env var (default 2, range [0,10]), while all others stay fail-fast via retries=0 default.
